gaps.sentence: His ___ (BEHAVE) at school has improved enormously.
The sky began to ___ as the storm approached (DARK).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -en forms the verb: darken means to become dark. A base verb follows 'to'.

gaps.sentence: Her ___ (PERFORM) in the final was outstanding.
gaps.explanation: After 'Her' a noun is needed: performance (-ance noun); performers are people.

gaps.sentence: There was a lot of ___ (OPPOSE) to the new road.
gaps.explanation: 'A lot of' needs a noun: opposition (-tion noun); 'opposite' is an adjective or noun meaning the contrary.

gaps.sentence: We ___ the cost of the trip and ran out of money (ESTIMATE).
gaps.hint: judged it too low — that is why the money ran out (under-)
gaps.explanation: Running out of money shows the estimate was too low: underestimated (under- + estimated).

gaps.sentence: The report highlighted the ___ of sport in schools (IMPORTANT).
gaps.explanation: After 'the' a noun is needed: importance (-ance).
After 'in' a noun is needed: excitement (-ment noun).

gaps.sentence: The article was full of ___ information (ACCURATE).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed before the noun 'information'
gaps.explanation: The negative adjective 'inaccurate' (in- + accurate) modifies the noun 'information'.
